statement.p: Compute the line integral of the vector field \mathbf{F}=\left\lt 3 y,-3 x\right> over the circle x^2+y^2=16 oriented clockwise

static.solution:
With r_0=4
The oriented path is parametrized by
\mathbf{c}(t)=(4\cos t,4\sin t); \quad t is changing from 2\pi to 0.
We compute the integrand: \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right) = \left\lt 3 y,- 3 x \right> = \left\lt 12 \sin t,-12 \cos t \right> \mathbf{c}'(t)= \left\lt -4 \sin t,4 \cos t \right> \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)\cdot {\mathbf{c}}'(t) = \left\lt 12 \sin t,-12 \cos t \right> \cdot \left\lt -4 \sin t,4 \cos t\right>=-48 \sin^2t -48\cos^2t =-48 Hence, \int_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{F} \cdot \,d\mathbf{\,s} = \int_{2\pi }^0 \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)\cdot {\mathbf{c}}'(t) \,dt= \int_{2\pi }^0 -48 \,dt=-48 t \bigg|_{2\pi}^0= 96 \pi
